input.quote: As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position. § 14.2 gives us ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for us and contains Vendor's present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest (plus equivalent assignments from its personnel). § 14.3 confirms Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined in § 1.8 as its pre-existing technology, excluding Customer Data and IP we owned before the Effective Date), and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the § 13.2 licence, which is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid, with modification and derivative-work rights for our business. § 14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data and that no right transfers to Vendor beyond a limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for us — service delivery, not independent exploitation — reinforced by § 15.1 (processing only on our documented instructions; no sale, advertising, data combination or model training without our express written consent). § 14.4 creates no joint ownership absent a separate signed instrument identifying exploitation rights, and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. Minor points noted but not flagged: § 14.2 conditions Deliverable ownership on payment of the applicable Fees, and § 15.1 includes an "as permitted by this Agreement" processing hook. Section 13.1's revocable Services licence is a LICENSE-rule issue and is not double-flagged here.
